title: Hashtags and hidden emails
description:
Write `final class Extract` with two static methods built on `java.util.regex`:

- `List<String> hashtags(String text)` returns the hashtags in order of first appearance, lower-cased, without the `#` and without duplicates. A hashtag is `#` followed by one or more letters, digits or `_`, and the `#` must not follow a letter or digit (so `C#` and `a#b` are not hashtags).
- `String maskEmails(String text)` replaces the part before the `@` of every email address with its first character and `***`: `ada.lovelace@example.com` becomes `a***@example.com`.
hints: A **negative look-behind** `(?<!X)` matches only where the text just before is *not* `X`, without taking any characters itself. `\p{L}` is any letter and `\p{N}` any digit, so `(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])#` means "a `#` not just after a letter or digit"; `(\\w+)` then takes the tag (lesson 8.01).
`matcher.replaceAll(r -> ...)` builds each replacement from the match; wrap it in `Matcher.quoteReplacement` so a `$` in the text cannot be read as a group reference.
